lines.name: Level: B1 · Topic: The Music Room

lines.text:
Learning to Play

Every Thursday afternoon, our school has music lessons in the music room. It is a large room on the ground floor with soundproof walls so the noise does not disturb other classes.

The music room has all kinds of instruments. Along one wall, there are acoustic guitars and electric guitars on stands. In the corner, there is an upright piano that our teacher, Mrs Clarke, plays beautifully. There are also drums, a xylophone, recorders, and a set of hand bells.

This term, we are learning about rhythm and melody. Mrs Clarke taught us to read basic musical notation — the symbols on a staff that tell you which notes to play and how long to hold them. A crotchet is one beat, a minim is two beats, and a semibreve is four beats.

We started by clapping rhythms together. Then, each student chose an instrument to practise. I chose the keyboard because I want to learn piano. My friend Tariq picked up the drums, and he was surprisingly good at keeping a steady beat.

At the end of the lesson, we played a simple piece together as a group. It was not perfect, but it sounded better than expected. Mrs Clarke said that playing in a group teaches you to listen to others and stay in time.

Next term, we will start preparing for the school concert. Each class will perform one piece. I am both excited and nervous. Music is one of my favourite subjects because it lets you express yourself without words.

lines.text: Music is part of the National Curriculum in England until age 14. Many schools have orchestras, choirs, and bands. Students can take GCSE and A-level Music exams. Peripatetic teachers visit schools to give individual instrument lessons.

lines.text: The BBC Proms (short for 'Promenade Concerts') is an annual summer festival of classical music held at the Royal Albert Hall in London. The Last Night of the Proms is a famous event broadcast on TV worldwide.
